rationale: HWS Math 331 Definition 1.2.1 gives the same three conditions in the same lower-set convention: '1. alpha is not empty and alpha != Q; 2. if p in alpha and q < p, then q in alpha; 3. if p in alpha, then there is some r in alpha such that r > p (i.e., alpha has no maximal element)' -- verbatim (C1), (C2), (C3). Wikipedia states the identical four conditions ('A is nonempty', 'A != Q', 'closed downwards', 'A does not contain a greatest element') and summarises them as 'a nonempty proper lower subset of Q with no maximal element'. The item's own Remarks fix the lower-set convention explicitly and note the upper-set alternative, so there is no convention ambiguity. Definition: no proof component.

HWS Definition 1.2.2: 'The set of real numbers R is the collection of all Dedekind cuts' -- the item's R := {A subseteq Q : A is a Dedekind cut}. The rational embedding q |-> q* = {r in Q : r < q} is HWS's r-hat (Theorem 1.2.5) and Wikipedia's 'the rational number q' identified with '{x in Q : x < q}'. Definition: no proof component. Its well-definedness obligation is discharged by lem-rational-cut-is-cut via justified_by.

HWS Theorem 1.2.5: 'For any rational number r the set r-hat = {q in Q : q < r} is a cut, and hence a real number.' That is the item's Statement exactly; the appended 'in particular 0* and 1* are cuts' is the same theorem instantiated at r = 0 and r = 1 (HWS Example 1.2.6 asks for exactly those cuts). Proof ai-altered: HWS supplies the three verification obligations as a guided outline and the item's steps 1.1-1.3 discharge precisely those with the standard q-1, transitivity and midpoint witnesses.

HWS Definition 1.2.9: 'For two real numbers (cuts) alpha and beta, we say alpha < beta if alpha subset beta. (The inclusion is proper, alpha != beta.)'; Wikipedia states the non-strict form 'x <= y <=> x subseteq y'. HWS Definition 1.2.12 defines positive and negative exactly as the item does ('alpha is positive if alpha > 0-hat and alpha is negative if alpha < 0-hat'). Convention deltas: the item additionally names nonnegative and nonpositive, and its Remarks record HWS Exercise 1.2.13.1 ('A cut alpha is positive if and only if 0 in alpha'). Definition: no proof component.

No source states this exact package. HWS Fact 1.1 gives only the substantive half ('If alpha and beta are cuts and alpha != beta, then either alpha subset beta or beta subset alpha (but not both)'), and Wikipedia records that 'The set of all Dedekind cuts is itself a linearly ordered set (of sets)'. The item merges totality with the reflexivity/antisymmetry/transitivity of set inclusion into one lemma: semantically identical content, reformulated and merged. Proof ai-altered: HWS's proof of Fact 1.1 ('Assume alpha != beta and alpha not-subset beta ... Let b in beta ... Since alpha not-subset beta, exists a in alpha so that a not-in beta ... So b < a. By cut property 2 for alpha, it follows that b in alpha') is step-for-step the item's steps 2.1-4.1.

The sum is exact: Wikipedia 'A + B := {a + b : a in A and b in B}', HWS Corollary 1.2.17 'alpha + beta = alpha (+) beta' with 'alpha (+) beta = {p + q : p in alpha, q in beta}'. The additive inverse is Girotti's '-alpha := {q in Q : exists r > 0 such that -q - r in U_alpha}', which is the item's formula once the two-sided cut's upper set U_alpha is rewritten as Q \ A in the lower-set convention; Wikipedia's '-B := {a - b : a < 0 and b in (Q \ B)}' is the same set. Tagged ai-altered rather than literature-derived because the item merges sum, additive identity, additive inverse and subtraction into a single definition and re-expresses the sourced inverse in the lower-set convention (the item itself records the equivalent form 'p in -A iff there is a rational s not in A with s < -p'). Definition: no proof component.

Every clause is sourced but no source states them as one lemma: HWS Theorem 1.2.16 (alpha + beta is a cut), Exercise 1.2.18 ('Addition of real numbers is commutative and associative'), Theorem 1.2.19 ('For any real number alpha, alpha + 0-hat = alpha'); Girotti's Step 3 checklist lists the same three obligations. ai-altered for the merge, not for any content change. Proof ai-altered: step 1.6 reproduces HWS Theorem 1.2.19's argument ('by property (3) there exists a rational s in alpha so that p < s. Then p - s < 0 ... p = s + (p - s)'), and steps 1.1-1.3 discharge HWS Theorem 1.2.16's three listed obligations.

Girotti states both halves with the item's exact inverse formula: '-alpha := {q in Q : exists r > 0 such that -q - r in U_alpha}' and '3. -alpha is the inverse of alpha for the sum, i.e. alpha + (-alpha) = 0 for all alpha in R'; HWS Theorem 1.2.24 ('Any real number alpha has an additive inverse') proves both that the inverse set is a cut and that alpha + beta = 0-hat. Statement therefore exact-source. Proof ai-altered: the item follows the standard integer-multiple boundary argument (greatest n with nw in A, then p = -(n+2)w and v = nw + p) rather than HWS's finite-list variant of the same idea.

Wikipedia: 'A x B := {a x b : a >= 0 and a in A and b >= 0 and b in B} union {x in Q : x < 0}'; Girotti gives the positive-case product, '1 := {q in Q : q < 1}', 'alpha^-1 := {q in Q : q > 0, exists r > 0 such that 1/q - r in U_alpha}', and the sign table (0 . alpha = 0; (-alpha)(-beta); -[(-alpha)beta]; -[alpha(-beta)]). Convention deltas recorded: the item writes the positive part with strict a > 0, b > 0 and unions {q <= 0} where Wikipedia uses a >= 0, b >= 0 and unions {x < 0} (the same set for positive cuts); it routes the sign extension through |A| rather than a three-row table; and its reciprocal witness form (s > 0, s not in A, p < 1/s) is Girotti's 1/q - r in U_alpha rewritten in the lower-set convention. One deliberate divergence, in the item's favour: the positive-case formula is restricted to strictly positive cuts, since at A = 0* the set {q <= 0} has greatest element 0 and is not a cut; zero products are supplied by the sign rule instead. Definition: no proof component.

Girotti states the property to be verified: '3. alpha^-1 is the inverse of alpha for the product, i.e. alpha . alpha^-1 = 1 for all alpha in R', with the reciprocal defined as above; Wikipedia gives the corresponding division formula. ai-altered because the item restates this in the lower-set/witness convention and strengthens it with the additional assertions that A^-1 is a cut and A^-1 > 0*. Proof ai-generated: both sources leave the verification as an exercise, and the item's argument (least n with a_0 y^n not in A, for y = 1/t and x < t < 1) is supplied locally. Checked in full: steps 1.1-3.1 close, and the reverse inclusion at step 3.1 produces the exact factorisation x = a . (x/a).

Girotti's Step 3 concludes '(R, +, .; <) is an ordered field', of which the field half is exactly this item's Statement; Wikipedia's construction-by-cuts section asserts the same. Rudin PMA Theorem 1.19 is the classical reference. Proof ai-generated: both located sources leave the field axioms as exercises, so the full sign-case distributivity argument (steps 1.5-10.1) is local. Read in full; it closes, though steps 2.1 and 3.2 argue general-sign associativity and commutativity by magnitude-and-sign matching rather than elementwise.

Girotti Step 2 records 'Q <-> {rational Dedekind cuts r = (L_r, U_r)} -> {Dedekind cuts} = R' with the map a bijection onto the rational cuts and an inclusion into R, and lists 'Q subset F' as a requirement of the construction; Wikipedia says the rationals embed by identifying q with {x in Q : x < q}; HWS Theorem 1.2.5 supplies that each q* is a cut. ai-altered because the item merges injectivity, order preservation AND reflection, the two ring identities, the unit identities, and density of the image into a single lemma, and no located source states that package; density of Q in R is classical (Rudin PMA Theorem 1.20(b)) but is there derived from the Archimedean property rather than from the cut model as here. Proof ai-generated: no source proof located for this packaging.

Wikipedia's ordered-field definition gives precisely the item's two compatibility clauses in precisely its non-strict form: 'if a <= b then a + c <= b + c' and 'if 0 <= a and 0 <= b then 0 <= a . b', together with a total order on a field. Girotti's Step 3 concludes '(R, +, .; <) is an ordered field' for the cut model specifically. Proof ai-generated: the sources leave the verification as an exercise; steps 1.1-2.1 are local and close.

Wikipedia's axiom of Archimedes for an ordered field K reads 'Let x be any element of K. Then there exists a natural number n such that n > x'; the item is that statement instantiated in the cut model, with the natural number replaced by its rational cut n*. ai-altered rather than literature-derived because of that model-specific reformulation and the added cofinality rephrasing ('no single cut is an upper bound for all of them'). Proof ai-generated: the three-line argument through a rational q not in A is local.

Wikipedia states the item's Statement essentially verbatim: 'If a nonempty set S of real numbers has any upper bound in R, then it has a least upper bound in R that is equal to union S' -- including the explicit identification of the supremum with the union, which is the item's distinguishing content. Wikipedia's Dedekind cut article likewise records that 'the set of Dedekind cuts has the least-upper-bound property'. Proof ai-altered: Girotti's Step 4 proof is the same three moves in the same order (the union is a cut; it is an upper bound; any upper bound contains it), transposed from the two-sided (L, U) presentation to the lower-set convention.

The construction is verbatim in the sources. Wikipedia: 'A = { a in Q : a^2 < 2 or a < 0 }', presented as the cut representing sqrt(2); HWS Exercise 1.2.7.3: 'Jim suggests: Does sqrt(2) = {q in Q : q^2 < 2 or q < 0} work?'; Girotti Example 6 uses L_alpha := {q in Q : q < 0} union {q in Q : q > 0, q^2 < 2} and says 'A posteriori (once we'll be done with the construction of R), we can say that alpha is actually the number sqrt(2)'. Proof ai-altered: the explicit witnesses r = (2q+2)/(q+2) and s = (2p+2)/(p+2) are the classical Rudin Example 1.1 witnesses (q - (q^2-2)/(q+2)); I recognise the argument as standard but could not fetch a verified URL carrying that text, so the proof is not tagged literature-derived. See the findings file: the title and prose call S 'the real number sqrt(2)' while the verification establishes only that S is a cut distinct from every rational cut.

Not an invented claim: the false statement is the verbatim negation of a sourced cut axiom -- HWS Definition 1.2.1.3 'alpha has no maximal element' and Wikipedia's 'A does not contain a greatest element'. The refuting construction is likewise standard: 0* is the rational cut 0-hat of HWS Example 1.2.6 and Theorem 1.2.5. Tagged ai-altered because the false-statement packaging (asserting the negation in order to refute it) is a local reformulation of established material, not a new mathematical claim; no generation.role is required since the statement is not ai-generated. Proof ai-altered: the refutation is HWS Theorem 1.2.5's verification specialised to r = 0, plus the observation that (C3) refutes the claim for every cut.
